 FROM THE PRINCIPAL'S DESK


     Welcome to Damdama College, Kulhati Kamrup. I wish to express my gratefulness to all the
members of the college community for giving me the opportunity to serve the college. The college
was established by the local community on 9th of August,1978 with an aim to provide higher
education to the upcoming generations and to make them self-reliant as well as competent citizens
of the nation.
    The college intends to translate these in to reality through teaching, learning, evaluation,
innovation, research and extension. The college pledges to enlighten rural poor by making them
aware of the global changes through education and co-curricular activities.
    Public Funded institutions like our college will obviously face some challenges in maintaining the
quality and standard of higher education under the recent wave of changes in economic as well as
educational policies of a global world. Therefore, it is the right time for all of us to come forward and
work together to face these challenges. I hope our sincere efforts will make this college a Centre of

     1.    A BRIEF HISTORY OF THE COLLEGE
      Damdama College, established on August 9, 1978, in the historic town of Hajo, Assam, has developed into a respected
academic institution. Situated in the vibrant area of Kulhati, the college spans 44 bighas and offers access via well-connected
roads. The nearest railway station is Kamakhya Railway Junction, approximately 31 km away, while Lokapriya Gopinath Bordoloi
International Airport at Borjhar is located about 38 km from the campus.

      In its formative years, Damdama College attracted distinguished faculty, including Professor Dr. Gobinda Ch. Deka, a
prominent scientist, and the late Professor Tarinikanta Bhattacharya, former Principal of Cotton College, who inaugurated the
college's classes. Notably, contributions from local academic figures like Mr. Bonkim Sharma, the retired Principal of Damdama
H.S. School, and Mr. Pramod Ch. Deva Sharma Shastri significantly fostered a culture of democratic and liberal humanism within
the institution.

      A historical overview of the college includes its initial dependence on Damdama H.S. School, which permitted college
students to utilize its classrooms for lectures. Classes commenced on January 2, 1982, in improvised settings as faculty and
students gathered bamboo and other materials to create temporary facilities. Degree courses were initiated under Gauhati
University in 1984, and the institution was designated a Grants-in-Aid college in 1989, followed by provincialization in 2005.
Recently, in March 2023, the college was evaluated by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), achieving a
B grade in its second cycle of assessment.

      The college’s strength lies in its academic excellence and supportive environment, catering to local students predominantly
from agro-based working-class backgrounds. This necessitates a nuanced managerial approach to foster growth and
development. A dedicated faculty, along with committed non-teaching personnel, creates a nurturing environment that enables
students to harness their potential in an intellectually vibrant atmosphere. The college strives to provide holistic education aimed
at empowering students as global citizens.

 6. RESERVATION RULES
1. There is a provision for reservation of seats, as per Government of Assam rules for the candidates
    belonging to the State of Assam. In this respect, caste certificate issued by the competent
    authority under Government of Assam only shall be valid
2. A maximum 5% of the total seats may be earmarked for students having outstanding performance
    in Extra Curricular Activities (Sports/Cultural/NCC/ Scouts & Guides) and wards of employees of
    the College. A screening committee is formed by the College to select the candidates for admission
    under ECA category.
3. There is a provision of reservation of 3% of the total seats for 'Differently abled' candidates under
    PWD category. Candidates seeking admission under ECA and PWD categories must produce
    his/her original documents on a date to be notified later after admission




7. ADMISSION PROCEDURE
Students have to register through the Samarth Portal (assamadmission.samarth.ac.in). The
admission procedure through Samarth Portal is as mentioned below and is directed by the DHE,
Assam.


    1. Registration through the Samarth Portal using mobile number.
    2. Fill the Profile (The students have to fill up their profile details correctly before the final submission).
         The candidate should have a valid email id and mobile no for registration. This email id and mobile no
         will be used for future communication. Upload passport size photograph and scanned signature
    3. Candidate has to fill Bank account details like Bank name, Branch name, Account number and IFSC
         number in the online form.
    4. Program Selection (College and Program selection will be available after the declaration of H.S result).
    5. The college will scrutinize the filled-up details of students and prepare merit list as per intake capacity
         and DHE order.

Damdama College has a central library and two reading rooms i.e. one for students and one for

Damdama College has a special library corner for local literature. Each academic year, the college

23.CELLS AND CLUB
1.Anti-Ragging Cell
The Anti-Ragging Cell at Damdama College has been established as a proactive initiative to prevent and
address any incidents of ragging or bullying, which are considered serious criminal offenses in India. These
acts can result in severe consequences, including imprisonment for a duration of two to ten years, substantial
fines, and strict academic penalties for the perpetrators. The primary goal of this cell is to create a safe and
supportive environment on campus, ensuring that all students can pursue their education free from the fear
of ragging. By actively monitoring and addressing potential incidents, the Anti-Ragging Cell is committed
to fostering a culture of respect and camaraderie among students, making the college campus a welcoming
and secure place for every Student.




                                                      25
 2.Cell Against Sexual Harassment
 Damdama College’s Cell Against Sexual Harassment is designed to address and combat sexual harassment
on the campus of the educational institution. This cell focuses on creating awareness, offering support to
victims, implementing preventive measures, and establishing clear policies. It serves as a safe space for
students to report incidents, seek guidance, and find legal and emotional support. Additionally, the initiative
often includes training programs and workshops to educate individuals on recognising and preventing
sexual harassment, promoting a culture of respect and safety.

3. Minority Cell
The presence of a Minority Cell at Damdama College is crucial in promoting social justice, equality, and
inclusion. The Cell plays a vital role in advocating for the rights of students belonging to minority
communities, promoting cultural heritage, and fostering an inclusive environment within the broader
society.

 4.     Scheduled Tribe /Scheduled Caste Cell
 The college has SC/ST & minority cell for the upliftment of the SC and ST community students and
 minority students of the college to bring awareness for the SC and ST community & minority students
 about their rights and benefits

5.      Entrepreneur Development Cell (EDC)
Entrepreneur Development Cell (EDC) of Damdama College is a dedicated initiative aimed at fostering
entrepreneurship among students and aspiring entrepreneurs. The cell provides various resources and
support systems, including mentorship programs, workshops, and training sessions designed to equip
individuals with essential skills in business management, innovation, and startup development. By
facilitating networking opportunities with industry experts, investors, and other entrepreneurs, the EDC
plays a crucial role in nurturing entrepreneurial talent, encouraging creativity, and promoting the launch of
new ventures. Additionally, the cell often organises competitions, seminars, and events that serve as
platforms for individuals to showcase their business ideas and receive constructive feedback. Overall, the
Entrepreneur Development Cell is pivotal in creating an ecosystem that empowers the next generation of
entrepreneurs. The cell constitutes of two convenor and Principal of the college and H.O.D of each
department of the college as members of the cell


6.      Women's Cell
The Damdama College Women's Cell addresses issues related to women's rights, empowerment, and
welfare. Its primary aim is to promote gender equality, provide support to Women Co-workers and students,
and create a safe environment for them. By addressing women's issues, the women's cell at Damdama
College contributes to community progress and fosters an environment where women can thrive. It also
catalyses social change by challenging stereotypes and promoting women's leadership across various fields.
The Damdama College Women's Cell plays a vital role in advocating for women's rights, empowerment,
and awareness. It is dedicated to providing comprehensive support to all women within the college through
the organisation of seminars and awareness programs focused on women's issues.

     7. Study Circle




Damdama College boasts a vibrant study circle, a dedicated club that fosters an enriching atmosphere of
knowledge and education among its students. This distinctive platform invites participants to immerse
themselves in the realm of literature, examining a variety of genres and articulating their reflections through
poetry. These expressions are showcased within the framework of "Dalichar Mell," a monthly academic
exercise held in a relaxed atmosphere, commonly referred to as "Adda." By promoting these activities, the
study circle aims to nurture and cultivate each student's innate creativity and intellectual curiosity, creating
a dynamic community where ideas can flourish and friendships can grow. By fostering these activities, the
study circle seeks to enhance the intellectual and artistic development of its members, thereby cultivating a
community that values both knowledge and self-expression.

    9. Career Counselling and Guidance Cell

    coordinator and two teachers of the college as members.
